title: Message creation lacked conversation membership validation
description: The original create rule required only an active sender matching the caller. Membership and body limits existed only in MessagingService. onMessageCreate trusts stored messages and sends notifications to conversation participants.
impact: Unauthorized message insertion, notification harassment and unbounded input into the push trigger. Does not imply disclosure of existing messages.
scenario: An active outsider knowing a conversation ID could submit their own message into it directly through Firestore.
patch: Implemented: require an existing conversation containing the caller, string body length 1–4000 and server creation/update timestamps. Follow up with schema validation, trigger membership/type checks, bounded token batches and idempotent delivery.
compatibility: Normal shared sendMessage writes already meet these requirements. Custom import clients using client timestamps now fail. Backend Admin writes bypass rules.
verification: New emulator tests allow student/facilitator members and deny outsiders, inactive accounts, forged senders, missing conversations, malformed/oversized bodies and missing timestamps.

title: Conversation attachments exposed to unrelated active users
description: Original attachment reads/writes were allowed to every active account; deletes to every active facilitator/admin. The path included a conversation ID but rules did not use its membership.
impact: Cross-conversation attachment disclosure, replacement and deletion through authenticated Storage requests.
scenario: An unrelated active account knowing the object path could download or replace a private attachment.
patch: Implemented: conversation-member read/write, explicit admin read, and member facilitator/admin delete. Admin delete remains allowed. Check legacy download-token URLs separately.
compatibility: Existing paths remain unchanged. Legitimate nonparticipant access is intentionally denied. Cross-service Storage-to-Firestore permissions must be enabled for the release environment; no live configuration was changed.
verification: Storage emulator accepted member upload/read and denied outsider download/replacement. Rules compiled and loaded. Download-token URL revocation and live IAM were not tested.

title: Availability queries disclose private appointment records
description: Any active student may read requested/accepted appointments with a string facilitator ID. getActiveByDateRange downloads full records and filters dates locally. Firestore cannot redact fields within a permitted document.
impact: Exposure of other students’ identities, notes and any additional private fields in active appointment documents.
scenario: A student queries active appointments for another student’s facilitator and receives private notes.
patch: Approve a minimal availability projection containing only facilitator ID, interval and occupancy. Backfill without notes/identities, migrate web/mobile readers, preserve reservation transactions, then restrict private reads to the student, facilitator and admin. Use a trusted writer or rigorously validated atomic projection on Spark.
compatibility: Requires collection/index/rules and client query migration; changing only reads breaks booking availability. Backfill and dual-read rollout are required.
verification: Isolated test reproduced unrelated-student read with a synthetic note. After migration invert this test and verify availability and concurrent booking.

title: Students control assessment risk metadata and submission integrity
description: Students can supply arbitrary risk fields when creating/updating in-progress attempts; create does not restrict all fields. Updates exclude only score/feedback, not risk metadata. assessment_responses may remain editable after submission. submitAttempt computes risk in the client, and generateAssessmentSummary trusts stored overallRiskLevel/overallRiskScore while recomputing domain scores. Student-created legacy assessments also have broad in-progress updates. Client alert creation can fail because risk_alerts create requires staff access.
impact: Manipulated screening risk, inconsistent clinical summaries, missing alerts and altered submitted response records; trusted scoring is not guaranteed.
scenario: A student bypasses client evaluation and submits arbitrary low-risk metadata, or modifies separately stored responses after submission.
patch: Approve a trusted submission/scoring transaction with typed question/value validation, publication checks, immutable submitted answers and authoritative risk/alert generation. Recompute all risk fields for AI prompts and statistics; remove student control of derived fields. Audit existing records before treating stored risk as authoritative.
compatibility: Backend scoring/alerts can require a billing/runtime architecture change for Spark. Maintain deterministic attempt IDs, limits and retakes. Existing records need reconciliation, not blind recalculation/deletion.
verification: Emulator accepted a synthetic student-supplied low-risk classification. Require denial of derived-field edits, atomic alerts and matching web/mobile/server scores after migration.

title: Authenticated clients can forge notifications for arbitrary recipients
description: Notification create requires authentication only. The recipient, title, body, type and related object are not authorized or bounded. Owner updates also allow changing recipient/content. Legitimate messaging, booking and assessment code currently creates cross-user notifications on clients.
impact: Misleading privileged-looking messages, harassment and storage/UI abuse; no proven code execution.
scenario: An authenticated outsider writes a synthetic notification addressed to a different user.
patch: Use trusted notification generation or rule-validated atomic events that bind sender, recipient and related entity via getAfter. Restrict owner updates to read-state/timestamps with immutable recipient; validate schema and length.
compatibility: Denying all cross-user create immediately breaks existing notifications. Migrate each producer and verify booking acceptance/rescheduling and messaging delivery.
verification: Emulator reproduced an outsider notification write. Invert after migration and test all legitimate producers.

title: Legacy appointment-slot reservations permit unrelated record tampering
description: A student can change an available slot to reserved with any string appointmentId, without restricting changed fields or verifying an owned appointment. Facilitator slot updates do not preserve facilitatorId either. The new Spark booking reservations are separately protected.
impact: Legacy slot poisoning, changed facilitator/time data and reduced availability. Does not establish bypass of the protected appointment_reservations workflow.
scenario: A student reserves an arbitrary available slot with a nonexistent appointment while changing its owner and start time.
patch: Inventory legacy consumers. If still used, bind reservation to an owned appointment in the same transaction with getAfter and immutable owner/time; otherwise explicitly retire student slot writes after client migration.
compatibility: Legacy mobile/slot-based clients may rely on this route; do not remove before identifying consumers.
verification: Emulator reproduced reservation with nonexistent appointment and altered ownership/time. Verify atomic linkage and immutable fields after migration.

title: Device-token updates could take over another owner’s document
description: The original create/update condition checked only the new uid. An attacker could replace a known token document and rewrite its uid to their own.
impact: Push registration corruption and notification denial. The flaw alone did not expose the victim’s token through reads.
scenario: An authenticated user overwrites another user’s predictable uid_platform token document, supplying their own uid.
patch: Implemented: active-user creation; updates require the existing owner and unchanged uid. Follow up with token schema/length limits and explicit account-switch cleanup.
compatibility: Normal uid_platform registration can still create and refresh its own document. Inactive account registrations now fail.
verification: Emulator allowed own creation/refresh, denied outsider takeover and denied inactive refresh.

title: Facilitators could rewrite schedule ownership
description: Schedule update authorized against only the previous facilitatorId, allowing the current owner to assign the schedule to another identity.
impact: Schedule poisoning or misattribution affecting another facilitator’s displayed availability.
scenario: A facilitator edits their own schedule and supplies a different facilitatorId.
patch: Implemented: require unchanged facilitatorId during updates. Follow up with server-enforced weekday/time schema and overlap checks.
compatibility: Normal same-owner schedule edits are preserved. Client ownership transfer is intentionally rejected.
verification: Emulator accepted an own weekday edit and rejected an ownership transfer.

title: Assignment and resource file access ignores record-level visibility
description: Assignment files can be read by any active user and deleted by any facilitator. Resource files are readable by any active user regardless of Firestore resource audience/isActive. Course files also do not honor unpublished status. These rules differ from restricted submission/resource metadata access.
impact: Assignment privacy loss and access to unpublished or role-restricted files through known object paths; unrelated facilitator deletion.
scenario: An active student obtains an assignment object path or a facilitator-only resource path and requests its bytes directly.
patch: Approve ownership/assigned-facilitator checks for assignment reads/deletes; mirror resource audience/publication checks and course publication/management permissions through Firestore documents. Classify legacy objects and revoke long-lived download tokens if required.
compatibility: Legacy assignments/course ownership policy must be defined; some resource entries may be missing metadata. Existing token URLs have a separate authorization lifecycle.
verification: Confirmed directly from allow conditions and contrasting metadata rules, not an executed download from live storage. Require positive/negative Storage emulator tests for each audience and relationship.

title: Deactivation does not consistently remove owner access
description: Firestore isOwner requires authentication but not active status. It authorizes users/profiles owner reads, notification access and some profile updates. Client session building rejects inactive accounts, but existing Firebase tokens can call rules directly. Storage owner checks originally had the same gap.
impact: Deactivated users retain selected reads/writes while their Auth session is valid. Most role-based collection access correctly requires isActive.
scenario: An inactive user keeps their token and reads their own profile outside the portal.
patch: Implemented active-account Storage ownership check. Approve per-operation Firestore active checks that preserve initial registration and document reads needed to report deactivation; consider Auth disable/revocation and tested revoked-token enforcement.
compatibility: Changing global Firestore isOwner risks registration/session discovery. Firebase password reset already revokes refresh tokens automatically; do not infer a password-reset revocation bug from a missing explicit call.
verification: Storage emulator denied inactive avatar upload; Firestore emulator reproduced inactive profile read. Full deactivation remains unresolved.

title: Historical dependency advisories require fresh validation
description: Repository audit snapshots dated 2026-10-12 flag workspace 71 packages (2 critical/48 high/21 moderate), Functions 10 (2 high/8 moderate), root 5 (4 high/1 moderate). Fresh npm audits failed to reach the registry. Installed/locked versions are recorded in evidence. Package counts overlap and do not establish application exploitability.
impact: Possible compromised or vulnerable tooling/runtime dependencies; severity is provisional pending fresh advisory and reachability analysis.
scenario: A vulnerable dependency is exercised by build tooling or runtime input if its affected code is reachable.
patch: Rerun audit with registry access for all three lockfiles and separate production/build/mobile exposure. Upgrade Functions/Admin and Expo/React Native/Vite in tested stages; avoid audit fix --force. Remove tracked root node_modules in a separately reviewed cleanup and reinstall from lockfiles.
compatibility: Historical suggested upgrades include major versions; Expo/native compatibility and Functions Node runtime need review. No dependencies were changed.
verification: Fresh audits returned errors, not clean results. Rerun full and omit=dev audits; verify advisory ranges, release builds, emulators and device builds.

title: Hosting configuration omitted browser defense headers
description: Repository Hosting config originally had no explicit framing, MIME-sniffing or referrer defenses. Actual deployed headers were not inspected. No successful XSS or clickjacking attack was demonstrated.
impact: Reduced browser protection against framing and MIME confusion.
scenario: A hostile page attempts to frame the portal when no other deployed framing policy exists.
patch: Implemented X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and CSP frame-ancestors/object-src/base-uri. Develop a full CSP in report-only mode after inventorying Firebase, Google Fonts, YouTube and other required origins.
compatibility: Embedding the portal is blocked; outbound YouTube frames are unaffected by frame-ancestors. Current CSP does not restrict script-src or connect-src.
verification: One local configuration test passed; web build passed. Live header delivery needs verification after an authorized deployment.

title: Privileged service-account files present locally; exposure not established
description: Two local service-account files contain private-key indicators and are untracked/ignored. Maintenance scripts read local credentials and may query or mutate the live project. No key validity, IAM grants, history exposure or filesystem ACL was checked. First-party tracked-source heuristics found zero secret indicators.
impact: A stolen valid Admin credential could bypass client rules within its IAM privileges. Presence of a local key is not proof of leaked credentials.
scenario: An attacker with local file or backup access obtains a key that remains valid.
patch: Inventory key owners, usage, IAM grants, ACLs and backup distribution; prefer short-lived ADC/workload identity. Rotate only if exposure is confirmed or owner approves. Keep migrations explicitly targeted, dry-run-first and gated; never copy keys into reports.
compatibility: Credential rotation and IAM edits can interrupt maintenance/deployments and were not performed. No production migration script was executed.
verification: Sanitized evidence records paths and boolean indicators only. Review history and provider key inventory through an authorized operational review.

title: AI summary regeneration lacks application-level abuse controls
description: Assigned staff/admin authorization and caching exist, but force=true bypasses cache. No per-user budget, durable rate limit or App Check enforcement is configured in source; concurrent requests can each invoke the provider. Provider/infrastructure quotas are unverified.
impact: Authorized or compromised staff accounts could increase AI spend, provider load and latency.
scenario: A permitted staff session repeatedly requests forced summaries for its assigned attempts.
patch: Add a durable per-actor/attempt cooldown, single-flight generation lease, explicit regeneration authorization and budgets. Integrate App Check only after configuring web/mobile clients; preserve staff assignment checks.
compatibility: App Check-only server enablement breaks clients without attestations. Rate controls must span function instances; an in-memory limiter is insufficient.
verification: Static source evidence only; no provider calls or load testing. Test rate/lease behavior against a stub and concurrent isolated requests.
